sections.history: Ambar Makalam, also called Thirumakalam, lies about 3 km from Poonthottam on the Tiruvarur–Mayiladuthurai road, in Tiruvarur district, on the southern bank of the Kaveri. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. By tradition only three temples carry the name Makalam — the famous Mahakaleshwar of Ujjain, the shrine at Irumbai near Pondicherry, and Ambar Makalam — which places this modest village temple in exalted company. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later. The village of Ambar also holds the Brahmapureeswarar temple, another Paadal Petra Sthalam.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Mahakalanathar in the sanctum, with the goddess Pachaiyambikai — also recorded as Bhakshayambikai and Rajamathangi — in her own shrine, a Nandi, and the parivara devatas. As the name Mahakala suggests, the lord is worshipped here in his aspect as the conqueror of time and death, and Devi is venerated in her powerful Shakti form.
sections.legends: The name Mahakala, 'the great time,' belongs to Shiva as lord over kaala — time itself, and so over death — the same aspect honoured at the great Mahakaleshwar of Ujjain. Tradition links the three Makalam shrines as a set, so that the pilgrim who reaches Ambar Makalam stands at the southern member of a rare and powerful trio. The goddess's fierce protective names, Bhakshayambikai and Rajamathangi, mark her Shakti grace at this place.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, honouring the Mahakala aspect especially on nights of Shivaratri. Pilgrims seeking the rare Makalam shrines and the Paadal Petra temples of the delta come to Ambar.
sections.experience: At Ambar Makalam the pilgrim meets Shiva in his most awe-inspiring aspect, Mahakala, the lord of time and death, in a quiet village shrine that shares its sacred name with distant Ujjain. Before Mahakalanathar and Pachaiyambikai, the visitor feels the gravity of a small temple that carries a great name — one of only three Makalams, kept alive on the southern bank of the Kaveri.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Ambar Makalam is about 3 km from Poonthottam on the Tiruvarur–Mayiladuthurai road, around 21 km from Tiruvarur and 25 km from Mayiladuthurai. Tiruvarur and Mayiladuthurai are the nearest rail heads, with buses via Poonthottam and local taxis to the village.
